full_judgment: 2. Facts of Civil Revision No. 3257 of 2003 as placed before the High Court Division, are that Dr. Ashequr Rahman, the Respondent No. 1 in Civil Petition No. 1498 of 2007 and the petitioner in Civil Petition No. 1333 of 2008, instituted Preemption Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1998 against Maha Maya Rani Saha, the petitioners both in Civil Petition Nos. 1498 and 1499 of 2007 and respondent No. 1 in Civil Petition No. 1333 of 2008, On the averments that in CS Dag No. 3123 Altabuddin owned 05-decimal of viti l and in Khatian No. 1590, Kafiluddin owned 05-decimals of land in CS Khatian No. 1591, Ukiluddin owned 05 decimal land in CS Khatian Nos. 1592, Lektunnessa and Badrunnessa owned 04 decimals of viti land in Khatian No. 1593, Shorforaj Uddin Kazi owned 05 decimal land in Khatian No. 1594 and in the said CS Dag No. 3123, out of 53 decimals land, 27 decimals were recorded in the names of the above persons and the remaining 26 decimals were recorded in the names of Shatish Chandra and Roshik Chandra, two brothers, in khatian No. 1588 who possessed their lands in ejmali; Lektonnessa was survived with husband Shakhawat Chowdhury, brothers Kafiluddin Kazi and Shorforaj Uddin Kazi, sister Badrunnessa and mother Ayesha Khatoon and that Shakhawat Chowdhury gifted his share in the above land inherited from his wife to other successors; Kazi Shamsul Huda and Ajimunnessa, respectively the son and wife of Altabuddin, and Jamordonnessa Sakinabad and Omdatunnessa, three daughters of Altabuddin, by registered patta dated 19-8-1924, by purchasing 22 decimals of lands from Khatian Nos. 1591, 1592, 1593, 1594 and 1595 became the absolute owners of 27 decimals of land and possessed the said land in ejmali along with the co-owners of the remaining 26 decimals of lands CS Dag No. 3123 and also the co- owners of CS Dag Nos. 3134 and 4223, subsequently by amicable settlement Kazi Shamsul Huda and others owned and possessed the entire 16 annals land in Dag No. 3123 and Jotish Chandra Rabri got the land in Dag No. 4123; Kazi Shamsul Huda, in the year 1348 BS, settled his entire 27 decimals land to his wife Jibonnessa, Dr Ashiqur Rahman, Anwara Khatoon and Shahjadi Begum and they having been possessing the said land by paying rent their names were recorded in SA Khatian No. 1090 in respect of the lands of Dag Nos. 3123, 360 and 4011 and the balance 26 decimal land of Dag No. 3123 was recorded in the Khas Khatian of the Government; SA recorded owner Shahjadi Begum sold her land to Dr Ashequr Rahman in the year 1980; in the year 1977, Kazi Shamsul Huda, by paying arrear rents of 22 years of the remaining 26 decimals of land of Dag No. 3123 which was recorded in Khas Khatian, also took lease of the same in the name of his wife Jibonnessa and planted trees therein, after the death of Kazi Shamsul Huda, his wife Jibonnessa, formed Kazi Shamsul Huda Trust vide registered deed No. 20169 dated 6-12-1982 and included 63 decimals of viti land of Dag No. 3123 in the above trust deed and appointed the Dr Ataur Rahman Khan, the pro- forma respondent No.2, as the Managing Trustee of the above trust; then Dr Ashequr Rahman, with the consent of Jebonnessa, used to possess the said land as a co-sharer and he is still in possession of the same and his name has been recorded in last SA Khatian No. 1090 and thereby he became co-sharer of the case land and it is only on 12-1-1998 he, for the first time, came to know that the respondent No. 1, on 16-4-1998, purchased the case land from the proforma respondent No.4 and that the respondent No.1, by filling Title Suit No.7 of 1990 also obtained decree therein in her favour in respect of the above khas khatian land; then on 22-1-1998, he on obtaining the certified copy of the said judgment and decree of the above said suit then on 16-4-1998, he after obtaining the certified copy of the deed of sale dated 23-9-1981 which was subsequently amended vide deed No. 3828 dated 31-7-1991, came to know about the sale of the case land; before selling the case land, the proforma respondent No.4 never informed him (Dr Ashequr Rahman) or other co-sharer about the sale and further neither the proforma respondent No. 4 nor the respondent No. 1 was ever in possession -of the case land and that the respondent No. 1 also did not make him (Dr Ashe- qur Rahman) a party in the above Title Suit No.7 of 1990. The respondent No. 1 contested the above miscellaneous case by filing written objection denying the material allegations made therein and con- tending that the total land in Dag No-3223 is 53 decimals out of which 26 decimals belonged to Roshik Chandra and Satish Chandra and the rest 27 decimals land were divided into 6 Khatians being numbers 1591-1595 in the names of Altabuddin and others; subsequently Roshik Chandra died leaving behind son Jogesh Chandra and Shatish Chandra died leaving being son Haripada; mistakenly the heirs of Jogesh Chandra got the land of Dag No. 3123 and subsequently Haripada died leaving only the cousin Jogesh and Jogesh died leaving behind wife Shovarani, the proforma respondent No.4, and another daughter; while in possession of the suit land, the proforma respondent No.4 sold her entire property including the 26 decimals of land, the suit land, to the respondent No.1 and she is the owner and possessor of the land; since the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Sreenagar threatened to lease out the suit land to others, she had file Title Suit No. 7 of 1990 and she obtained decree therein and the Government did not prefer Appeal against it and then she took steps for mutation of the case land on payment of rent, which is pending before the Additional Commissioner (Revenue); the" pre-emptor Dr Ashequr Rahman was never in possession of the case land and the Government also never possessed the case land. The learned Assistant Judge, after hearing by judgment and Order dated 31-5- 2000 dismissed the miscellaneous case. On Appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal Nos. 38 with 41 of 2000, the learned District Judge, after hearing by judgment and Order dated 15-4-2003 also dismissed the Appeal. The pre-emptor then moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 3257 of 2003 and after hearing, the High Court Division, by the impugned Order made the Rule absolute.
